name: default
_about: The shipped, brand-neutral defaults. Code reads its numbers from here; skills point here instead of restating them.
Your brand does NOT go in this file. `capcutctl profile init` writes ~/.config/capcutctl/profile.json from
profile.template.json; that file merges over this one, holds only what you change, and never enters the repo.
`capcutctl profile where` lists the layers; `capcutctl profile` prints the merged result.
The engine numbers (camera, density, grammar) were measured from the original author's library (see
`provenance`); the colours below are placeholders chosen to look unfinished until you set your own.

color._note: Roles, not hues: brand is the fill behind white text (hook block, CTA chip); accent is the ONE key word. Set yours in the user profile.

ease._note: Linear only for counters and progress. Camera keeps the harvested FreeCurveInOut.

scene._note: Full-frame motion-design scenes (mograph/scenes, docs/mograph.md#scenes). Scenes name colour ROLES, never hex: change a role here and every scene follows. brand/accent/ink mirror tokens.color.

brand._about: Who the videos are from and the rules that make them feel like one channel. Skills read this section; the engine does not. Fill it in your user profile.
rules: One accent per piece, on at most one element per shot, never on a title or a large fill.
Structure comes from scale, weight, spacing and luminance, not from glow, gradients or drop shadows.
Every graphic serves a spoken beat: it starts on the word and is gone when the idea is.
Real material over illustration, illustration over stock: captured UI, real numbers, real frames.

styles._about: How the brand flexes per video type. Pick one per video (edit.json `style`). A style sets pace and emphasis; it is NOT a set of scenes. Add styles in your user profile, change any field, or set one to null to drop it.

explainer.use: An opinion, a lesson, an argument: the face carries it.
explainer.feel: Typographic and calm. Big words, lots of empty frame, one visual idea.
explainer.accent: the one word the argument turns on
explainer.camera: slow pushes on the claims; no punches
explainer.sound: sparse: a cue on each graphic, nothing in between

demo.use: A tool or workflow shown on screen.
demo.feel: Fast and precise. The capture is the picture; graphics label it, never cover it.
demo.accent: the control or result the viewer must find
demo.camera: punches and callouts on the capture; the face stays 1x
demo.sound: clicks and ticks on the UI; one impact on the result

product.use: A physical object: a review, an unboxing, a comparison.
product.feel: Tactile and deliberate. Real numbers, the object itself, fewer and bigger moves.
product.accent: the number or feature that decides it
product.camera: holds on the object; one push on the verdict
product.sound: weighty: thuds on numbers, a reveal on the verdict

news.feel: Urgent and dense. The name lands first, then what changed, then why it matters.
news.accent: the name of the thing, once
news.camera: snap punch on the hook; stress pushes on each change
news.sound: an impact on the name, pops on each change

safeZones._note: Canvas pixels, y down. Platform UI covers the top bar, the caption/CTA band and the right action rail.

logo._note: The measured 0.13s pop with its pop cue. `--motion RECIPE` and `--glow` are opt-in; native motion recipes are experimental.

motion._note: Native text recipes; mirror tokens.color.brand / accent without the #.

captions._note: No full subtitles by default. 1-3 word keyword supers are part of the grammar.

never: anything that spins or loops forever
letter-by-letter Arabic, or Arabic set in a Latin fallback face
text that repeats the whole spoken sentence
a graphic without a sound, or a sound without a reason on screen
the same template twice within 10 seconds
camera motion on the circle layout
anything inside the platform UI zones
a punch and a callout on the same target
an endcard longer than 3 seconds with nothing new on it

provenance._note: Measured from the original author's hand edits across 88 drafts (2026-08-26). Evidence for the engine defaults, not targets.
provenance.animationsInLibrary: 3 of 1493 material_animations were real (hand edits were hard-cut); the target is now highly animated
